may_be_looking_for: People aged 15 to 70 with symptomatic lupus meeting American Rheumatism Association criteria
may_exclude_people_who: People who require tetracycline or other photosensitizing drugs
patient_summary: This study looks at how ultraviolet A-1 (UVA-1) light therapy may affect people with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and healthy volunteers. Researchers want to understand the mechanisms of this therapy.
patient_title: Ultraviolet A-1 Light Therapy for Lupus
questions_to_ask_clinician: What are the potential risks and benefits of UVA-1 light therapy for lupus?
Is there any special preparation needed before receiving UVA-1 light therapy?
Are there alternative treatments available for lupus?
source_grounding: title: Ultraviolet Light Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
brief_summary: OBJECTIVES: I. Evaluate the mechanisms of ultraviolet A-1 light therapy in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and normal controls.

eligibility_excerpt: PROTOCOL ENTRY CRITERIA: --Disease Characteristics-- Patients ages 15 to 70 with symptomatic systemic lupus erythematosus meeting American Rheumatism Association criteria and normal controls --Prior/Concurrent Therapy-- No requirement for tetracycline or other photosensitizing drugs
uncertainty_notes: The study status is listed as unknown, so it is unclear if results are available or if the study is still recruiting.
what_researchers_are_studying: The researchers are studying the effects of ultraviolet A-1 light treatment on the immune system and symptoms in people with lupus and in healthy individuals.
